evidence.text: PRKX is selectively inhibited by type I regulatory subunits PRKAR1A and PRKAR1B but not by type II subunits PRKAR2A/PRKAR2B. This distinguishes PRKX from PRKACA, which associates with both RI and RII. The RI-selective binding means PJA1-mediated degradation of PRKAR1A directly de-represses PRKX

PRKAR1B (type I-beta regulatory subunit) inhibits PRKX catalytic activity by forming a holoenzyme complex. PRKX is selective for RI subunits and does not interact with RII subunits (PRKAR2A/PRKAR2B), unlike the classical PRKACA catalytic subunit

PRKX promotes neuronal differentiation via cAMP-dependent signalling; drives renal epithelial tubulogenesis and neurite outgrowth in model systems. Aberrant recombination between PRKX (Xp22.3) and PRKY (Yp11.3) causes XX male sex reversal, underscoring the functional non-equivalence of these paralogs despite high sequence identity
